plain.text: Therefore, there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. Through Christ, the law of the Spirit who gives life has set us free from the law of sin and death. God did what the law could not do: he sent his own Son in a human body like ours to deal with sin. Those who live by the Spirit set their minds on what the Spirit desires. The mind set on the flesh leads to death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace. If the Spirit of God, who raised Jesus from the dead, lives in you, he will also give life to your mortal bodies.

So we have an obligation, not to live by our sinful nature, but by the Spirit. Those who are led by the Spirit of God are children of God. You did not receive a spirit that makes you a fearful slave again, but the Spirit of adoption, by whom we cry, "Abba, Father." The Spirit himself testifies with our spirit that we are God's children, and if children, then heirs, heirs of God and co-heirs with Christ, if we share in his sufferings so we may also share in his glory.

Paul considers that our present sufferings are not worth comparing with the glory that will be revealed. The whole creation waits eagerly. It has been groaning as in the pains of childbirth, waiting to be set free from decay. We also groan inwardly as we wait for our full adoption, the redemption of our bodies. We are saved in this hope. And the Spirit helps us in our weakness. When we do not know what to pray, the Spirit himself intercedes for us with groans that words cannot express.

"We know that God works all things together for the good of those who love him, who are called according to his purpose." Those God foreknew, he also predestined to be like his Son; those he called, he also justified and glorified. "If God is for us, who can be against us?" He did not spare his own Son but gave him up for us all; will he not also graciously give us all things? Who will bring any charge against God's chosen ones? Christ Jesus, who died and was raised, is at God's right hand, interceding for us.

Who shall separate us from the love of Christ? Trouble, hardship, persecution, hunger, danger, or the sword? In all these things we are more than conquerors through him who loved us. Paul is convinced that neither death nor life, neither angels nor rulers, neither the present nor the future, nor any powers, neither height nor depth, nor anything else in all creation, will be able to separate us from the love of God that is in Christ Jesus our Lord.

summary.bigIdea: In Christ there is no condemnation, the Spirit makes us God's children, and nothing can separate us from God's love.
points: "There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus."
The Spirit helps us pray and assures us we are God's children.
"If God is for us, who can be against us?" Nothing can separate us from his love.
summary.reflection: Read verses 38–39 slowly. Which of the things Paul lists do you most need to hear cannot separate you from God's love?
